test_title: PYST 23: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Articles was introduced by the 86th Amendment to impose a duty on parents to educate children?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A(k)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 51A(k)** was introduced by the **86th Amendment Act, 2002** of the Constitution of India.
 
• It imposes a **fundamental duty on parents or guardians** to provide opportunities for education to their children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• The amendment aligns with the provisions of **Article 21A**, which guarantees free and compulsory education for children in the same age group.
 
• Article 51A(k) is part of the **Fundamental Duties** under Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It emphasizes the shared responsibility of parents and the state in ensuring access to education for children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**:

 
 
• It inserted **Article 21A**, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It amended **Article 45**, focusing on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.
 
• It added **Article 51A(k)** under Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**:
 
 
• Guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It places the responsibility on the state to provide access to elementary education.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties in India**:
 
 
• Listed under Part IVA of the Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• Initially, ten duties were introduced by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• The 11th duty (Article 51A(k)) was added by the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009**:
 
 
• Enacted to operationalize Article 21A.
 
• Mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Ensures the infrastructure, teacher training, and quality education in schools.
